objective_for_doctor: Assess and diagnose the patient presenting with a 1-year history of worsening shortness of breath and weight loss.

turns.doctor_opening: Hello, what brings you in today? Could you tell me about yourself and what's been going on?
turns.patient_opening: Doctor: Hello, what brings you in today? Patient: I’m a 56-year-old man, and over the past year my shortness of breath has been steadily getting worse, along with weight loss. I used to work construction and in a steel mill earlier in life, and I’m still an active smoker.

turns.doctor_question: Do you often find yourself needing to rush to the bathroom to urinate, or feeling like you have to go right away?
turns.patient_answer: Patient: No, I haven’t noticed any urgency or needing to rush to the bathroom to urinate.

turns.doctor_question: Have you noticed any firm lumps or masses in your breast tissue, either while showering, getting dressed, or during self-exams?
turns.patient_answer: Patient: No, I haven’t noticed any firm lumps or masses in breast tissue, and I haven’t had any unusual changes during self-exams.

turns.doctor_question: Have you noticed any small, firm bumps on your skin that are smooth to the touch?
turns.patient_answer: Patient: I haven’t noticed any small, firm bumps on my skin that feel smooth to the touch.

turns.doctor_question: been reviewing your symptoms, and I want to ask: Have you been feeling like you just can't seem to cool down or catch your breath, even when you're in a cool environment or not exerting yourself much
turns.patient_answer: Patient: No, I don’t feel overly hot or like I can’t cool down, and I don’t have trouble catching my breath when I’m not exerting myself. The main issue is that my shortness of breath has been steadily getting worse over the past year.

turns.doctor_question: How have you been feeling lately? Have you been experiencing a lot of pressure or anxiety in your daily life?
turns.patient_answer: Patient: I’ve been feeling progressively more short of breath with daily activities, but I wouldn’t say I have a lot of pressure or anxiety day to day. I’ve also lost some weight over the past year.

turns.doctor_question: Have you been experiencing any itching or a sensation that makes you want to scratch, either on specific areas of your body or all over?
turns.patient_answer: Patient: I haven’t noticed any itching or a sensation that makes me want to scratch anywhere on my body.

turns.doctor_question: Have you noticed any unusual spots, rashes, or lesions along the veins on your arms?
turns.patient_answer: Doctor: Have you noticed any unusual spots, rashes, or lesions along the veins on your arms? Patient: No, I haven’t noticed any unusual spots, rashes, or lesions along the veins in my arms.

turns.doctor_question: Have you noticed any trouble finding the right words when you're talking, like trying to think of a word but it just won't come to you?
turns.patient_answer: Patient: No, I haven’t noticed any trouble finding the right words or feeling unusually confused. My main problem is that my shortness of breath has been steadily getting worse with everyday activities, along with the weight loss.

turns.doctor_question: Have you noticed any stiffness or tension in your muscles, perhaps feeling like your muscles are hard to relax or move, even when you're not using them?
turns.patient_answer: Patient: No, I haven’t noticed any stiffness or hard-to-relax muscle tension. I mainly just feel progressively more short of breath with my daily activities, and I’ve lost some weight over the past year.

turns.doctor_question: How are you feeling today in terms of your energy levels and alertness? Do you feel unusually drowsy or tired?
turns.patient_answer: Patient: I feel pretty alert overall, but my energy has been lower than before because the shortness of breath makes it hard to do my normal daily activities. I don’t feel unusually drowsy or out of it.

turns.doctor_question: Do you feel that one or both of your legs are unusually warm right now, or do they feel about the same temperature as the rest of your body?
turns.patient_answer: Patient: No, my legs feel about the same temperature as the rest of my body, not unusually warm. I haven’t noticed any temperature difference between my legs and the rest of me.

turns.doctor_question: Do you find that you're coughing up mucus or phlegm, or is your cough mostly dry?
turns.patient_answer: Patient: I don’t really have a cough or any phlegm that I can say. It’s mainly the steadily worsening shortness of breath with my daily activities and the weight loss.
